title: Grandma Rosie's Smash Burger
tagline: A crisp-edged, juicy burger with the kind of cheese pull that ends the conversation.
image_credit: Original AI-generated food image created for this edition.
equipment: 12-inch cast-iron or heavy skillet, sturdy spatula, parchment paper
ingredients: 1 tsp neutral oil, for the pan
1 tsp pickle brine, plus dill pickles to serve

steps.title: Mix the Rosie sauce
steps.text: Stir the mayonnaise, ketchup, mustard, and pickle brine together. Set it near the stove so the burgers can be assembled while hot.

steps.title: Toast the buns
steps.text: Heat the dry skillet over medium heat. Toast the cut sides of the buns until golden, about 45 seconds. Set aside.

steps.title: Smash for the crust
steps.text: Raise the heat to high and add the oil. Divide beef into four loose balls. Working one at a time, place a ball in the pan, cover with parchment, and press firmly with a sturdy spatula until about 1/4 inch (6 mm) thick. Season with salt and pepper.

steps.title: Flip and melt
steps.text: Cook without moving for 1 1/2 to 2 minutes, until the edges are deeply browned. Scrape underneath, flip, add a slice of cheese, and cook 45 to 60 seconds more, until the beef reaches 160°F (71°C) and the cheese melts.

steps.title: Build the burger
steps.text: Spread sauce on the buns, add the hot patty and pickles, close the bun, and serve right away. For a double, stack two patties per bun.

rosie_tip: Don't pack the beef into a tight meatball. Loose beef makes the lacy, crispy edges that a thick patty can only dream about.
storage: Best eaten immediately. Refrigerate cooked patties in a sealed container for up to 3 days; reheat in a skillet until steaming hot.
serve_with: Serve with crinkle-cut fries, a dill pickle, and extra Rosie sauce.
photo_caption: The finished burger: browned edges, melted cheese, and a little Rosie sauce.

visual_steps.label: PREP
visual_steps.text: Mix the quick sauce; portion cold beef.

visual_steps.label: SEAR
visual_steps.text: Smash in a hot pan; add cheese.

visual_steps.label: BUILD
visual_steps.text: Stack bun, patty, pickles, and sauce.

title: Three-Ingredient Stovetop Mac & Cheese
tagline: Creamy, cozy, and made without a powdered orange packet in sight.
image_credit: Original AI-generated food image created for this edition.
equipment: Medium heavy-bottomed saucepan, wooden spoon, box grater
ingredients: 3 cups (720 ml) whole milk, plus a splash if needed
2 cups (200 g) sharp cheddar, freshly grated
Kosher salt, optional and not counted among the three main ingredients

steps.title: Warm the pasta and milk
steps.text: Put the macaroni and milk in a heavy saucepan. Bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat, stirring often and scraping the corners so nothing sticks.

steps.title: Cook until just tender
steps.text: Keep the milk at a quiet simmer, never a hard boil. Cook 9 to 12 minutes, stirring every 30 seconds, until the pasta is al dente and most of the milk has thickened around it.

steps.title: Make it cheesy
steps.text: Turn off the heat. Add the cheddar in three handfuls, stirring until each addition melts before adding the next. Taste and add a small pinch of salt if the cheese needs it.

steps.title: Rest and serve
steps.text: Let the pot stand for 2 minutes; the sauce will cling to the noodles as it settles. If it becomes too thick, stir in warm milk 1 tablespoon at a time.

rosie_tip: Grate the cheese yourself. Pre-shredded cheese is coated to keep it separate, and that coating can make a silky sauce turn grainy.
storage: Refrigerate for up to 3 days. Reheat gently on the stove with 1 to 2 tablespoons of milk per serving; do not boil.
serve_with: Add a green salad or roasted broccoli if you want to pretend this is a balanced dinner. I won't tell.
photo_caption: A spoonable bowl of creamy cheddar macaroni, ready to serve.

visual_steps.label: START
visual_steps.text: Add dry pasta and milk to the pot.

visual_steps.label: SIMMER
visual_steps.text: Stir often until just tender.

visual_steps.label: FINISH
visual_steps.text: Fold in cheddar until glossy.

title: Air-Fryer Crispy Chicken Tenders
tagline: Crunchy, tender, and ready for a dunk in honey mustard.
image_credit: Original AI-generated food image created for this edition.
equipment: Air fryer, three shallow bowls, instant-read thermometer
ingredients: For dipping: 1/4 cup mayonnaise, 1 tbsp honey, and 1 tsp Dijon mustard

steps.title: Season the chicken
steps.text: Pat the tenders dry. Whisk the buttermilk and egg in one bowl. In a second bowl, combine flour, paprika, garlic powder, salt, and pepper. Put panko in a third bowl.

steps.title: Bread each tender
steps.text: Coat a piece of chicken in seasoned flour, dip it in the buttermilk mixture, then press it into the panko. Set on a rack and repeat. Let the coating sit for 5 minutes so it adheres.

steps.title: Air-fry in batches
steps.text: Heat the air fryer to 400°F (200°C). Arrange tenders in one layer with space between them; spray the tops lightly with oil. Cook 10 to 12 minutes, turning once, until deeply golden and 165°F (74°C) inside.

steps.title: Stir the dip
steps.text: While the chicken cooks, stir mayonnaise, honey, and Dijon together. Add a pinch of salt if desired. Serve the tenders hot with the dip.

rosie_tip: If the basket is crowded, the coating steams instead of crisping. Give each tender a little personal space; even chicken needs boundaries.
storage: Refrigerate for up to 3 days. Re-crisp in an air fryer at 350°F (175°C) for 3 to 5 minutes; avoid microwaving if you want to keep the crunch.
serve_with: Try honey mustard, ranch, barbecue sauce, or a squeeze of lemon with crunchy slaw.
photo_caption: Golden panko tenders with honey mustard for dipping.

visual_steps.label: BREAD
visual_steps.text: Set up flour, buttermilk, and panko.

visual_steps.label: AIR-FRY
visual_steps.text: Cook in one layer until crisp.

visual_steps.label: SERVE
visual_steps.text: Pair golden tenders with the dip.

title: Fluffy American Buttermilk Pancakes
tagline: Tall, tender pancakes with crisp buttery edges and real maple syrup.
image_credit: Original AI-generated food image created for this edition.
equipment: Two mixing bowls, whisk, nonstick skillet or griddle
ingredients: 3 tbsp (42 g) unsalted butter, melted and cooled
Butter and maple syrup, for serving

steps.title: Whisk the dry ingredients
steps.text: In a large bowl, whisk the flour, sugar, baking powder, baking soda, and salt until evenly combined.

steps.title: Mix the wet ingredients
steps.text: In another bowl, whisk the buttermilk, egg, melted butter, and vanilla. Pour into the dry ingredients and fold just until no dry flour remains. A few small lumps are welcome.

steps.title: Heat the griddle
steps.text: Warm a lightly buttered skillet over medium heat, about 350°F (175°C). A drop of water should dance and disappear, not smoke.

steps.title: Cook the pancakes
steps.text: Pour 1/4 cup (60 ml) batter for each pancake. Cook until bubbles appear and the edges look set, about 2 minutes. Flip once and cook 1 to 2 minutes more until golden and springy.

steps.title: Serve warm
steps.text: Stack the pancakes, add butter, and drizzle with maple syrup. Keep finished pancakes on a rack in a 200°F (95°C) oven while you cook the rest.

rosie_tip: Stop mixing when the flour disappears. Smooth batter makes flat pancakes; a few lumps make the tall, fluffy ones.
storage: Refrigerate cooked pancakes for up to 3 days or freeze between parchment sheets for 2 months. Reheat in a toaster or a 300°F (150°C) oven.
serve_with: Fresh berries, sliced bananas, crisp bacon, or a spoonful of peanut butter all feel right at the breakfast table.
photo_caption: A tall stack with melting butter and maple syrup.

visual_steps.label: MIX
visual_steps.text: Whisk wet and dry bowls separately.

visual_steps.label: GRIDDLE
visual_steps.text: Flip when bubbles set on top.

visual_steps.label: STACK
visual_steps.text: Add butter and warm maple syrup.

title: Bacon, Egg & Cheese Breakfast Sandwich
tagline: The diner-counter classic you can make before the coffee gets cold.
image_credit: Original AI-generated food image created for this edition.
equipment: Large skillet, small nonstick skillet, paper towels

steps.title: Cook the bacon
steps.text: Place bacon in a cold skillet and set over medium heat. Cook, turning as needed, until crisp, 8 to 10 minutes. Transfer to paper towels and pour off all but 1 teaspoon of the drippings.

steps.title: Toast the muffins
steps.text: Toast the English muffins cut-side down in the same skillet until golden, 1 to 2 minutes. Keep warm.

steps.title: Fry the eggs
steps.text: Melt the butter in a nonstick skillet over medium-low heat. Crack in the eggs, season lightly, and cook until the whites are fully set and the yolks are cooked to your preference. For a neat stack, break the yolks and fold each egg into a square; cook until no liquid egg remains.

steps.title: Melt and stack
steps.text: Place a slice of cheese on each hot egg for 30 seconds. Set the eggs on the toasted muffin bottoms, add two bacon slices, close the sandwiches, and serve.

rosie_tip: Low heat gives you tender eggs. High heat gives you a rubber coaster with ambitions.
storage: For meal prep, cool the cooked eggs and bacon completely, then refrigerate separately for up to 3 days. Assemble and reheat just before eating.
serve_with: Add a sliced tomato, a little hot sauce, or a hash-brown patty tucked right inside.
photo_caption: Toasted muffin, folded egg, bacon, and melted American cheese.

visual_steps.label: PREP
visual_steps.text: Cook bacon and toast the muffins.

visual_steps.label: FRY
visual_steps.text: Set eggs gently in a skillet.

visual_steps.label: STACK
visual_steps.text: Layer egg, cheese, and bacon.

title: Cheesy Weeknight Beef Tacos
tagline: Seasoned beef, crunchy shells, and enough cheddar to make Tuesday feel festive.
image_credit: Original AI-generated food image created for this edition.
equipment: Large skillet, sheet pan, small bowls for toppings
ingredients: 1 cup shredded lettuce, 1 diced tomato, and sour cream, for topping

steps.title: Brown the beef
steps.text: Heat a skillet over medium-high. Add the beef and cook, breaking it into small crumbles, until no pink remains and the meat reaches 160°F (71°C), about 6 to 8 minutes. Drain excess fat if needed.

steps.title: Season and simmer
steps.text: Stir in chili powder, cumin, paprika, garlic powder, salt, and water. Simmer uncovered for 4 to 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until glossy and lightly saucy.

steps.title: Warm the shells
steps.text: Arrange taco shells on a sheet pan and warm according to the package directions, usually 3 to 5 minutes at 350°F (175°C).

steps.title: Fill and finish
steps.text: Divide the beef among the shells. Top with cheddar, lettuce, tomato, and sour cream. Serve at once while the shells are crisp.

rosie_tip: Let the beef simmer with the spices for a few minutes. A packet dumped over dry meat is not a seasoning strategy; it's a cry for help.
storage: Refrigerate the beef separately for up to 3 days. Reheat until steaming hot, then fill freshly warmed shells so they stay crunchy.
serve_with: Set out salsa, lime wedges, pickled jalapeños, and guacamole so everyone can build their own.
photo_caption: Crunchy shells loaded with seasoned beef, cheddar, lettuce, and tomato.

visual_steps.label: BROWN
visual_steps.text: Break beef into small crumbles.

visual_steps.label: SIMMER
visual_steps.text: Add spices and a splash of water.

visual_steps.label: FILL

title: Garlic-Butter Pizza Bread
tagline: Crispy baguette, garlicky butter, marinara, and bubbling mozzarella.
image_credit: Original AI-generated food image created for this edition.
equipment: Rimmed sheet pan, small bowl, sharp bread knife

steps.title: Heat the oven
steps.text: Set a rack in the center and heat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Line a sheet pan with parchment.

steps.title: Make garlic butter
steps.text: Stir the softened butter, grated garlic, and Italian seasoning together. Split the baguette lengthwise and place cut-side up on the pan.

steps.title: Toast the bread
steps.text: Spread the garlic butter over the cut surfaces. Bake 4 to 5 minutes, just until the edges begin to crisp. This quick toast helps keep the bread from turning soggy.

steps.title: Top and bake
steps.text: Spoon marinara over the bread, leaving a narrow border. Scatter mozzarella and Parmesan evenly. Bake 8 to 10 minutes, until the cheese bubbles and the edges are golden.

steps.title: Slice and serve
steps.text: Rest 2 minutes, add basil, and cut into thick pieces with a serrated knife.

rosie_tip: Toast the bread before adding sauce. Soggy pizza bread is just a very confused sponge.
storage: Store leftovers in the refrigerator for up to 2 days. Reheat on a sheet pan at 375°F (190°C) for 6 to 8 minutes; the microwave softens the crust.
serve_with: A bowl of marinara for dipping and a simple green salad make this a proper lunch.
photo_caption: Baguette halves with garlic butter, red sauce, and browned mozzarella.

visual_steps.label: PREP
visual_steps.text: Split baguette and spread garlic butter.

visual_steps.label: BAKE
visual_steps.text: Add sauce and cheese; bake bubbly.

visual_steps.label: SLICE
visual_steps.text: Top with basil and cut to share.

title: Loaded Cheesy Fries
tagline: Crispy fries, melted cheddar, smoky bacon, cool sour cream, and green onion.
image_credit: Original AI-generated food image created for this edition.
equipment: Sheet pan or air fryer, oven-safe serving dish, skillet
ingredients: 1 cup (100 g) sharp cheddar, freshly grated
4 strips bacon, cooked crisp and crumbled
1 small jalapeño, seeded and sliced, optional

steps.title: Crisp the fries
steps.text: Heat the oven to the temperature on the fry package, usually 425°F (220°C). Spread fries in a single layer on a preheated sheet pan and bake, turning once, until deeply golden and crisp, about 25 to 30 minutes. Air-fry in batches if preferred.

steps.title: Cook the bacon
steps.text: While the fries bake, cook bacon in a skillet over medium heat until crisp. Drain on paper towels, then crumble.

steps.title: Melt the cheese
steps.text: Pile the hot fries in an oven-safe dish. Scatter cheddar and bacon over the top. Return to the oven for 2 to 3 minutes, just until the cheese melts.

steps.title: Finish and share
steps.text: Dollop with sour cream and finish with green onions, jalapeño, and black pepper. Serve immediately with forks for the table.

rosie_tip: Crisp the fries first and add cheese second. If you cover them from the start, you get steamed potato sticks. Nobody ordered that.
storage: These are best straight from the oven. Refrigerate leftovers for up to 2 days and re-crisp uncovered at 400°F (200°C) for 8 to 10 minutes.
serve_with: Add ranch or barbecue sauce on the side. For a heartier plate, top with leftover taco beef or pulled chicken.
photo_caption: A shareable bowl of crisp fries with cheddar, bacon, sour cream, and chives.

visual_steps.label: CRISP
visual_steps.text: Bake fries in one even layer.

visual_steps.label: MELT
visual_steps.text: Add cheddar and bacon to hot fries.

visual_steps.label: FINISH
visual_steps.text: Dollop sour cream; scatter onions.

title: Crispy Two-Cheese Grilled Cheese
tagline: Buttery, golden bread around a blanket of stretchy cheddar and Monterey Jack.
image_credit: Original AI-generated food image created for this edition.
equipment: Large skillet or griddle, spatula, box grater
ingredients: 8 slices sourdough or sturdy white bread

steps.title: Build the sandwiches
steps.text: Mix cheddar and Monterey Jack. Spread butter on one side of each bread slice. Turn four slices butter-side down; spread a thin swipe of Dijon on the inside if using and add the cheese. Close with the remaining bread, butter-side out.

steps.title: Cook low and slow
steps.text: Heat a skillet over medium-low. Cook sandwiches in batches for 3 to 4 minutes per side, pressing gently with a spatula, until the bread is evenly golden.

steps.title: Let the cheese catch up
steps.text: If the bread is browning before the cheese melts, lower the heat and cover the skillet for 1 minute. Remove the lid for the last 30 seconds to keep the crust crisp.

steps.title: Slice and serve
steps.text: Rest each sandwich for 1 minute, then cut diagonally. Serve with hot tomato soup for dunking.

rosie_tip: Low heat is the secret. A sandwich is not late for work; give the cheese time to melt before you rush it.
storage: Grilled cheese is best fresh. If needed, cool and refrigerate for up to 1 day, then reheat in a dry skillet over low heat until crisp and hot.
serve_with: Classic tomato soup, dill pickles, or a handful of kettle chips.
photo_caption: Golden sourdough with melted cheese stretching between the halves.

visual_steps.label: BUILD
visual_steps.text: Butter bread; sandwich the cheese.

visual_steps.label: TOAST
visual_steps.text: Cook low until both sides are golden.

visual_steps.label: SLICE
visual_steps.text: Cut when the middle is stretchy.

title: Buffalo Chicken Crunch Wraps
tagline: Spicy chicken, cool ranch, crunchy lettuce, and plenty of cheddar in a toasted wrap.
image_credit: Original AI-generated food image created for this edition.
equipment: Small saucepan, large skillet or griddle, tongs
ingredients: 1/2 cup (120 ml) ranch or blue-cheese dressing

steps.title: Warm the Buffalo chicken
steps.text: Combine the cooked chicken and wing sauce in a small saucepan over medium-low heat. Stir until hot, about 3 minutes. Taste before adding extra salt; bottled sauce is already seasoned.

steps.title: Fill the tortillas
steps.text: Warm tortillas briefly in a dry skillet so they bend without cracking. Place chicken down the center of each, then add cheddar, lettuce, and a drizzle of dressing.

steps.title: Roll tightly
steps.text: Fold the sides inward, then roll from the bottom into a snug wrap. Keep the seam underneath.

steps.title: Toast and serve
steps.text: Melt butter in a skillet over medium. Cook wraps seam-side down for 2 minutes, then turn and toast the other side until golden and the cheese melts. Cut in half and serve with celery.

rosie_tip: Put the seam down first. Gravity is a free kitchen helper, and it keeps the good bits from escaping.
storage: For meal prep, keep the warm chicken separate from the lettuce and dressing. Refrigerate up to 3 days; assemble and toast just before serving.
serve_with: Celery sticks, carrot ribbons, and extra ranch for dipping.
photo_caption: A crisped tortilla wrap showing Buffalo chicken, lettuce, and ranch.

title: Loaded Baked Potatoes
tagline: Crisp skins, fluffy centers, melted cheddar, smoky bacon, and cool sour cream.
image_credit: Pexels stock photo, used under the Pexels License; attribution is optional.
equipment: Rimmed baking sheet, fork, small skillet
ingredients: 4 medium russet potatoes (about 8 oz / 225 g each)
4 strips bacon, cooked crisp and crumbled
2 tbsp sliced chives or green onions

steps.title: Heat and prep
steps.text: Heat the oven to 425°F (220°C). Scrub and dry the potatoes. Pierce each one 6 to 8 times with a fork so steam can escape.

steps.title: Bake until fluffy
steps.text: Rub the skins with olive oil and 1/2 teaspoon salt. Set potatoes directly on a rimmed baking sheet and bake 50 to 65 minutes, turning once, until a knife slides easily into the center.

steps.title: Cook the bacon
steps.text: While the potatoes bake, cook bacon in a skillet until crisp. Drain, cool slightly, and crumble.

steps.title: Fluff and load
steps.text: Cut a slit down each potato and squeeze the ends gently to open. Fluff the inside with a fork, add butter, then cheddar, bacon, sour cream, chives, the remaining salt, and pepper.

steps.title: Serve hot
steps.text: Return the loaded potatoes to the oven for 2 minutes if you want the cheese extra melty. Bring them to the table while the centers are still steaming.

rosie_tip: Dry the skins before oiling them. If the skin isn't crisp, the potato is still wearing its pajamas.
storage: Refrigerate un-topped baked potatoes for up to 4 days. Reheat at 375°F (190°C) until hot, then add fresh toppings. Do not leave cooked potatoes at room temperature for more than 2 hours.
serve_with: A bowl of chili, a simple salad, or grilled chicken turns one potato into dinner.
photo_caption: Loaded potato with cheddar, bacon, sour cream, and fresh chives; serving inspiration.

visual_steps.label: BAKE

visual_steps.label: LOAD

title: Creamy Garlic Parmesan Pasta
tagline: Silky fettuccine, mellow garlic, cream, and a snowfall of Parmesan.
image_credit: Pexels stock photo, used under the Pexels License; attribution is optional.
equipment: Large pot, 12-inch skillet, tongs, measuring cup for pasta water
ingredients: 1 cup (95 g) finely grated Parmesan, plus more to finish
1/2 cup (120 ml) reserved pasta water, as needed
1/2 tsp kosher salt, plus more for the pasta water

steps.title: Boil the pasta
steps.text: Bring a large pot of water to a boil and salt it until it tastes pleasantly seasoned. Cook fettuccine according to the package, stopping 1 minute before fully tender. Reserve 1 cup pasta water, then drain.

steps.title: Soften the garlic
steps.text: While the pasta cooks, melt butter in a large skillet over medium-low heat. Add garlic and cook 30 to 45 seconds, stirring constantly, until fragrant but not browned.

steps.title: Make the cream sauce
steps.text: Pour in the cream and bring to a gentle simmer. Cook 3 to 4 minutes, stirring, until slightly thickened. Lower the heat and whisk in Parmesan, salt, and pepper.

steps.title: Toss until glossy
steps.text: Add drained pasta and toss with tongs for 1 to 2 minutes. Add pasta water a splash at a time until the sauce coats every ribbon and looks silky.

steps.title: Finish and serve
steps.text: Taste for salt, scatter with parsley and extra Parmesan, and serve immediately. The sauce thickens as it stands, so keep a little pasta water nearby.

rosie_tip: Freshly grated Parmesan melts smoothly. The bagged stuff can clump up when it gets hot, and I don't need any more drama in this kitchen.
storage: Refrigerate for up to 3 days. Reheat gently in a skillet with a splash of milk or water, stirring until hot; do not let the cream sauce boil hard.
serve_with: Garlic bread and a crisp green salad are the classic partners.
photo_caption: Creamy fettuccine finished with Parmesan and herbs; serving inspiration.

visual_steps.text: Cook fettuccine; reserve pasta water.

title: Diner-Style Bacon Cheeseburgers
tagline: A thick, juicy patty, crisp bacon, sharp cheddar, and a toasted bun.
image_credit: Pexels stock photo, used under the Pexels License; attribution is optional.
equipment: Large skillet or grill, instant-read thermometer, paper towels
ingredients: 1 tbsp ketchup and 1 tsp yellow mustard

steps.title: Cook the bacon
steps.text: Cook bacon in a cold skillet over medium heat, turning until crisp, 8 to 10 minutes. Transfer to paper towels. Pour off the grease and wipe the skillet carefully.

steps.title: Shape the patties
steps.text: Divide beef into four portions and shape gently into patties about 4 1/2 inches (11 cm) wide. Press a shallow dimple in the center of each so it cooks evenly. Season both sides with salt and pepper.

steps.title: Sear and melt
steps.text: Heat the skillet over medium-high. Cook patties 3 to 4 minutes per side, without pressing them, until the center reaches 160°F (71°C). Add cheddar during the last minute and cover briefly to melt.

steps.title: Toast and assemble
steps.text: Toast the buns cut-side down in the skillet. Stir mayonnaise, ketchup, and mustard. Spread sauce on the buns, then add lettuce, tomato, the patty, and two bacon strips.

rosie_tip: Don't press a thick patty with your spatula. You want the juices in the burger, not decorating the pan.
storage: Refrigerate cooked patties and bacon separately for up to 3 days. Reheat patties to steaming hot and build fresh with lettuce and tomato.
serve_with: Shoestring fries, onion rings, or a crunchy dill-pickle spear.
photo_caption: A bacon cheeseburger stacked with cheddar and classic toppings; serving inspiration.

visual_steps.text: Shape thick patties; cook the bacon.

visual_steps.label: SEAR
visual_steps.text: Cook beef safely; melt cheddar on top.

visual_steps.label: BUILD
visual_steps.text: Stack lettuce, tomato, bacon, and sauce.

title: Philly-Style Cheesesteak Sandwiches
tagline: Thin-sliced beef, soft onions, and melted provolone tucked into warm rolls.
image_credit: Photo by jeffreyw via Wikimedia Commons, licensed CC BY 2.0. Full attribution is on the Image Credits page.
equipment: Large griddle or wide skillet, sharp knife, tongs
ingredients: 1 lb (450 g) ribeye, very thinly sliced
1 green bell pepper, thinly sliced, optional Rosie-style addition
1/2 tsp kosher salt and 1/4 tsp black pepper

steps.title: Make slicing easy
steps.text: If the steak is not already shaved, place it in the freezer for 20 to 25 minutes until firm but not frozen solid. Slice as thinly as possible across the grain.

steps.title: Soften the vegetables
steps.text: Heat half the oil on a griddle or in a wide skillet over medium-high. Add onion and optional pepper. Cook 5 to 7 minutes, stirring, until soft and lightly browned. Transfer to a plate.

steps.title: Sear the steak
steps.text: Add the remaining oil. Spread steak in a thin layer and season with salt and pepper. Sear 1 to 2 minutes, turn, then chop and fold with a spatula until just cooked through.

steps.title: Melt the cheese
steps.text: Return the vegetables to the pan. Divide the mixture into four piles, cover each with two slices of provolone, and cover the pan for 30 to 60 seconds until melted.

steps.title: Fill the rolls
steps.text: Butter and toast the rolls cut-side down. Use a spatula to lift each cheesy pile into a roll. Serve while the cheese is still stretchy.

rosie_tip: The beef has to be thin and the pan has to be hot. Peppers are my house-style addition; leave them out for a more traditional order.
storage: Refrigerate the cooked beef and onions for up to 3 days. Reheat in a skillet until steaming hot and fill fresh rolls; the bread is better toasted at the last minute.
serve_with: Kettle chips, a sharp pickle, or a small cup of beef jus for dipping.
photo_caption: A classic cheesesteak with thin beef, onions, and melted cheese; serving inspiration.

visual_steps.label: SLICE
visual_steps.text: Shave steak; slice onions thin.

visual_steps.label: SEAR
visual_steps.text: Brown beef fast; melt provolone.

visual_steps.label: FILL
visual_steps.text: Tuck the cheesy pile into warm rolls.

title: Classic Chocolate Chip Cookies
tagline: Crisp edges, soft centers, and chocolate in every bite.
image_credit: Pexels stock photo, used under the Pexels License; attribution is optional.
equipment: Stand mixer or hand mixer, two baking sheets, parchment paper, cookie scoop
ingredients: 3/4 cup (150 g) packed light brown sugar

steps.title: Whisk the dry mix
steps.text: In a bowl, whisk flour, baking soda, and salt. Set aside. Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C) and line two baking sheets with parchment.

steps.title: Cream butter and sugars
steps.text: Beat butter, brown sugar, and granulated sugar on medium speed for 2 minutes, until light and fluffy. Scrape the bowl. Beat in eggs one at a time, then vanilla.

steps.title: Finish the dough
steps.text: Add the flour mixture on low speed and mix just until combined. Fold in chocolate chips. Cover and chill the dough for 30 minutes; this keeps the cookies thicker and improves the flavor.

steps.title: Scoop and bake
steps.text: Scoop 2-tablespoon portions onto the sheets, leaving 2 inches (5 cm) between them. Bake one tray at a time for 10 to 12 minutes, until edges are golden and centers still look slightly soft.

steps.title: Cool patiently
steps.text: Sprinkle with flaky salt if you like. Let cookies rest on the tray for 5 minutes, then move to a rack. The centers finish setting as they cool.

rosie_tip: Pull the cookies while the centers still look a little underdone. Carryover heat finishes them; a clean toothpick would mean you waited too long.
storage: Keep baked cookies airtight at room temperature for 4 days. Freeze scooped dough balls for up to 2 months and bake from frozen, adding 1 to 2 minutes.
serve_with: A cold glass of milk, coffee, or a scoop of vanilla ice cream between two cookies.
photo_caption: Freshly baked chocolate chip cookies with soft, chocolatey centers; serving inspiration.

visual_steps.label: MIX
visual_steps.text: Cream butter and sugars; fold in chips.

visual_steps.label: BAKE
visual_steps.text: Bake until the edges are golden.

visual_steps.label: COOL
visual_steps.text: Let the centers set on a cooling rack.

title: Three-Ingredient Fudgy Brownies
tagline: A small-pan brownie with a shiny top and a rich, chewy center.
image_credit: Pexels stock photo, used under the Pexels License; attribution is optional.
equipment: 8-inch (20 cm) square pan, parchment paper, mixing bowl, whisk
ingredients: Flaky salt, optional; not counted among the three main ingredients

steps.title: Prepare the pan
steps.text: Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Line an 8-inch square pan with parchment, leaving two paper handles so the brownies lift out easily.

steps.title: Mix the batter
steps.text: Whisk the chocolate-hazelnut spread and eggs until glossy and smooth. Fold in the flour just until no dry streaks remain; overmixing makes a tougher brownie.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Spread the batter evenly into the pan. Bake 18 to 22 minutes, until the edges are set and a toothpick inserted near the center comes out with a few moist crumbs.

steps.title: Cool before slicing
steps.text: Sprinkle with flaky salt if desired. Cool in the pan for at least 30 minutes, then lift out and cut into 9 large or 12 smaller squares with a warm, clean knife.

rosie_tip: Brownies keep baking as they cool. If the toothpick comes out completely clean, you've gone one minute too far, dear.
storage: Store airtight at room temperature for 3 days or refrigerate for up to 1 week. For extra fudgy slices, chill for 30 minutes before cutting.
serve_with: Warm brownies with vanilla ice cream, or a little espresso if the grown-ups are staying up.
photo_caption: Rich chocolate brownies cut into neat squares; serving inspiration.

visual_steps.label: MIX
visual_steps.text: Whisk spread and eggs; fold in flour.

visual_steps.label: BAKE
visual_steps.text: Stop at moist crumbs on the tester.

visual_steps.label: SLICE
visual_steps.text: Cool fully; lift out and cut squares.

title: Chocolate Peanut Butter Cups
tagline: A crisp chocolate shell and a soft, salty-sweet peanut center.
image_credit: Pexels stock photo, used under the Pexels License; attribution is optional.
equipment: 12-cup mini muffin pan, paper liners, microwave-safe bowl, small spoon
ingredients: 10 oz (285 g) semisweet chocolate, finely chopped or chips
Flaky salt, optional for the tops

steps.title: Line the pan
steps.text: Place a paper liner in each cup of a mini muffin pan. Make room in the refrigerator or freezer for the pan to sit flat.

steps.title: Melt the chocolate
steps.text: Microwave the chocolate in a dry bowl in 20-second bursts, stirring each time, until smooth. Spoon about 1 teaspoon into each liner and tilt or brush it partway up the sides. Chill 5 to 8 minutes until firm.

steps.title: Mix the filling
steps.text: Stir peanut butter, powdered sugar, and optional fine salt until thick and smooth. Roll into 12 small balls and flatten each into a disk slightly smaller than the liners.

steps.title: Fill and cap
steps.text: Place a peanut-butter disk in each chocolate shell. Spoon remaining chocolate over the top to cover the filling. Tap the pan gently to level the tops.

steps.title: Chill until set
steps.text: Add a few flakes of salt if desired. Refrigerate 25 to 30 minutes, until firm. Peel away the liners and serve cool.

rosie_tip: Make sure the first chocolate layer reaches partway up the liner, or the peanut butter will try to escape out the sides.
storage: Keep covered in the refrigerator for up to 2 weeks, or freeze for up to 2 months. Let stand 5 minutes before eating for the softest center.
serve_with: A little bowl of berries or a cup of coffee balances the sweet chocolate.
photo_caption: Chocolate shells filled with peanut butter; serving inspiration.

visual_steps.label: MELT
visual_steps.text: Make a thin chocolate shell in liners.

visual_steps.label: FILL
visual_steps.text: Add peanut filling; cap with chocolate.

visual_steps.label: SET
visual_steps.text: Chill until firm, then peel the liners.

title: No-Bake Strawberry Cheesecake Cups
tagline: Cool cheesecake cream, buttery crumbs, and bright strawberries layered in little jars.
image_credit: Pexels stock photo, used under the Pexels License; attribution is optional.
equipment: Six 6-oz (180 ml) jars or glasses, hand mixer, two mixing bowls
ingredients: 1 1/2 cups (225 g) fresh strawberries, hulled and diced

steps.title: Make the crumb base
steps.text: Stir graham crumbs and melted butter until the mixture resembles damp sand. Divide among six jars and press gently with the back of a spoon.

steps.title: Whip the cheesecake cream
steps.text: Beat softened cream cheese, powdered sugar, and vanilla until smooth. In a second bowl, whip cold cream to medium-stiff peaks. Fold the whipped cream into the cream-cheese mixture in two additions.

steps.title: Prepare the berries
steps.text: Stir diced strawberries with jam and lemon juice. Let stand 5 minutes so the berries turn glossy and release a little juice.

steps.title: Layer the cups
steps.text: Spoon cheesecake cream over the crumb bases, add a layer of strawberries, then finish with another spoonful of cream and a few berries on top.

steps.title: Chill and serve
steps.text: Cover and refrigerate at least 2 hours, until the filling is cool and softly set. Keep chilled until serving.

rosie_tip: Use room-temperature cream cheese and cold heavy cream. One makes the filling smooth; the other gives it a lovely lift.
storage: Cover and refrigerate for up to 2 days. Add the final fresh strawberry garnish just before serving. Do not freeze in glass jars.
serve_with: A little lemon zest or a crisp shortbread cookie on the side.
photo_caption: Layered strawberry dessert cups with cream and biscuit crumbs; serving inspiration.

visual_steps.text: Press buttery graham crumbs into jars.

visual_steps.label: FOLD
visual_steps.text: Fold whipped cream into cream cheese.

visual_steps.label: LAYER
visual_steps.text: Add berries and cream; chill to set.

title: Sausage, Egg & Cheese Breakfast Burritos
tagline: A warm tortilla packed with fluffy eggs, breakfast sausage, crisp potatoes, and cheddar.
image_credit: Pexels stock photo, used under the Pexels License; attribution is optional.
equipment: Large skillet, nonstick skillet, spatula, foil for freezing
ingredients: 1/2 cup (120 ml) salsa, plus more to serve

steps.title: Brown the sausage
steps.text: Cook sausage in a large skillet over medium heat, breaking it into crumbles, until browned and 160°F (71°C), about 7 to 8 minutes. Transfer to a plate.

steps.title: Crisp the potatoes
steps.text: Add hash browns to the same skillet. Spread them in a thin layer and cook undisturbed for 3 to 4 minutes, then turn and cook until crisp and golden.

steps.title: Scramble the eggs
steps.text: Whisk eggs with milk, a pinch of salt, and pepper. Melt butter in a nonstick pan over medium-low. Add eggs and stir gently until soft curds form and no liquid egg remains.

steps.title: Fill and roll
steps.text: Warm tortillas briefly so they bend easily. Divide sausage, potatoes, eggs, cheddar, and salsa down the center of each. Fold in the sides and roll tightly from the bottom.

steps.title: Toast the seam
steps.text: Return burritos seam-side down to a dry skillet over medium heat. Toast 1 to 2 minutes per side until golden and sealed. Serve with extra salsa.

rosie_tip: Warm tortillas roll without cracking. Cold tortillas have stage fright, and I can't blame them.
storage: For freezing, leave out salsa, cool the fillings completely, roll, and wrap each burrito tightly in foil. Freeze up to 2 months. Reheat until the center reaches 165°F (74°C).
serve_with: Salsa, avocado, hot sauce, or a few orange slices for a diner-style breakfast plate.
photo_caption: A breakfast burrito with egg, cheese, sausage, and crisp potatoes; serving inspiration.

visual_steps.text: Brown sausage; crisp the hash browns.

visual_steps.label: SCRAMBLE

title: Cottage Cheese Crust Pizza
tagline: A tender, golden cottage-cheese dough topped with tomato sauce and bubbling mozzarella.
image_credit: Pexels stock photo, used under the Pexels License; attribution is optional.
equipment: Fine-mesh sieve, food processor or blender, mixing bowl, parchment, sheet pan
ingredients: 1 cup (225 g) cottage cheese, drained 10 minutes
1 1/4 cups (160 g) self-rising flour, plus extra for dusting
1/3 cup sliced mushrooms, bell pepper, or pepperoni

steps.title: Heat the oven and drain
steps.text: Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Set cottage cheese in a fine-mesh sieve for 10 minutes to remove excess liquid. Blend until smooth.

steps.title: Mix the dough
steps.text: Whisk the blended cottage cheese and egg together. Add self-rising flour and oregano; stir until a shaggy dough forms. Turn onto a floured surface and knead gently for 1 to 2 minutes. If it is very sticky, add flour 1 tablespoon at a time.

steps.title: Shape and par-bake
steps.text: Press or roll the dough on parchment into a 10-inch (25 cm) round, about 1/4 inch (6 mm) thick. Transfer parchment and dough to a sheet pan. Bake 14 to 16 minutes, until the surface looks set and the edge is lightly golden.

steps.title: Add the toppings
steps.text: Spread on pizza sauce, leaving a small border. Add mozzarella, chosen toppings, and Parmesan. Return to the oven for 7 to 9 minutes, until the cheese bubbles and the crust is golden underneath.

steps.title: Rest and slice
steps.text: Let the pizza stand for 3 minutes before slicing. The crust firms as it cools slightly. Add basil or red-pepper flakes if you like.

rosie_tip: Drain the cottage cheese first. Extra water is the enemy of a crisp crust, and the sieve is a lot easier than arguing with the oven.
storage: Refrigerate slices for up to 3 days. Reheat on a hot sheet pan or in a skillet until the crust is crisp and the center is steaming. Protein content varies by brand and serving size.
serve_with: A simple Caesar salad or crunchy vegetables. For another variation, add cooked chicken and spinach.
photo_caption: A golden cheese pizza; the cottage-cheese crust is a homemade variation.

visual_steps.text: Blend cottage cheese; mix soft dough.

visual_steps.label: BAKE
visual_steps.text: Par-bake crust, top, then bake again.

visual_steps.label: SLICE
